Social Constructivism · View of Learning
Cover.

THE CORE CLAIM

People learn by constructing knowledge —
not by receiving it.

Knowledge is not a copy of objective truth. It is built by people — through dialogue, interpretation, and reaching consensus within a community.

"'Truth' or 'reality' will be accorded only to those constructions on which most people of a social group agree." — Heylighen (1993, as cited in Adams, 2006, p. 246)

Your First-Person Choices Reveal:

Here are the three core roles in a social constructivist learning environment — and you just lived them from the inside: 你刚才的选择，正好展示了社会建构主义学习环境中的三个核心角色：

🧑‍🎓

The Learner 学习者

Active constructor of meaning — brings prior knowledge, cultural background, personal theories. Learns through dialogue, inquiry, and making. 意义建构者：带着已有知识、文化背景和自己的想法，在对话、探究和动手做中学习。

👩‍🏫

The Teacher 教师

Guide and scaffold — not an instructor. Organizes authentic tasks, asks open questions, operates in the learner's Zone of Proximal Development. 引导者与脚手架：设计真实任务、提开放问题，在学生的“最近发展区”里提供支持。

🏫

The Environment 环境

A social, collaborative space with authentic, worthwhile tasks. Peer interaction. Assessment embedded in learning, not a separate test. 社会协作的空间：真实有价值的任务、同伴互动，评估就发生在学习过程中。

ROLE · 1 OF 3

🧑‍🎓 The Learner

🧑‍🎓

Active
Constructor

not a passive receiver
The learner does not receive knowledge from a teacher — they construct it, building on prior knowledge and cultural background to make personal sense of new experiences.
What they bring
Implicit theories, cultural perspectives, personal meaning-making
How they learn
Dialogue, experimentation, cognitive conflict, peer collaboration
Motivation
Learning orientation (deep understanding) > performance orientation (grades)
What "failure" means
Not wrongness — less accurate prediction, ready to be revised
"Existing knowledge structures and beliefs support or militate against new learning… Individuals bring implicit theories and perspectives derived from the cultural milieu." (Adams, 2006, p. 249)
The Learner

ROLE · 2 OF 3

👩‍🏫 The Teacher

👩‍🏫

Guide &
Scaffold

not an instructor
The teacher does not transmit knowledge — they scaffold the learning journey, operating in the learner's Zone of Proximal Development.
Primary role
Organizer of environments, facilitator, information source when needed
How they interact
Open-ended questions, listener & observer, creates safety for cognitive conflict
What they design
Authentic, case-based learning tasks
Power dynamic
Gradually transfer the learning agenda to the learner
"The teacher's role is as facilitator… what is required is a paradigm shift: the abandonment of the familiar to embrace the new." (Brooks & Brooks, 1993, as cited in Adams, 2006, p. 250)
The Teacher

ROLE · 3 OF 3

🏫 The Environment

Learning does not happen in a vacuum. It is a social, collaborative space where dialogue is the engine.
Social space
Peer interaction scaffolds each other
Worthwhile tasks
Ends in themselves, connected to life-worlds
Assessment
Part of learning — not a separate test event
Cultural context
Home bridges to school — "common knowledge"
"Good assessment tasks are interchangeable with good instructional tasks." (Shepard, 2000, as cited in Adams, 2006)

So — how do people learn?

They learn by interacting — with people, with tasks, with the world — and co-constructing meaning together.

✅ Learner = active constructor
✅ Teacher = guide & scaffold
✅ Environment = social, authentic space
✅ Learning = consensus-building through dialogue
